user_stories.story: As a reviewer, I want every backend dependency pinned to an exact version so builds are reproducible.
As a deployer, I want the production backend image to install only runtime packages, with no test tools.
As a developer/CI, I want one requirements-dev.txt that gives me runtime plus test tooling.
As a maintainer, I want the Postgres image pinned to the same exact 16.x tag in docker-compose and CI.
As a maintainer, I want frontend installs (CI and Docker) to use the lockfile via npm ci.

acceptance_criteria.c: backend/requirements.txt contains only runtime packages: fastapi, uvicorn[standard], websockets, asyncpg, pydantic, pydantic-settings. Every non-blank line matches name==x.y.z (extras such as [standard] allowed). No >=, ~=, ^, or unpinned names. Pass: regex check over the file.
backend/requirements.txt does not contain pytest, pytest-asyncio, or httpx. Pass: grep finds none.
backend/requirements-dev.txt is new. It has `-r requirements.txt`, then pytest==x, pytest-asyncio==x, httpx==x. Every other line is name==x.y.z. Pass: regex check.

Every pinned version equals the version installed in the repo-root .venv. The implementer reads them with `pip freeze` / `pip show` from that venv for the 7 directly listed packages plus pytest and pytest-asyncio. No version is guessed or upgraded. Transitive dependencies are not pinned (see assumptions).
A fresh venv outside the repo, with `pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt`, runs `pytest` from backend/ green: 33 passed, 6 skipped when TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: the backend job runs `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`. cache-dependency-path covers requirements-dev.txt and requirements.txt. The frontend job runs `npm ci` instead of `npm install`. The file parses as valid YAML.

The postgres image in ci.yml and in docker-compose.yml is the same exact tag, `postgres:16.` (a current 16 minor chosen by the implementer; no bare `postgres:16`, no `latest`). Pass: the two image strings are identical.
backend/Dockerfile still installs only requirements.txt. This is verified and left unchanged unless a change is needed.
frontend/Dockerfile uses `npm ci`. It copies package-lock.json alongside package.json before the install, so npm ci can run.

README.md: the backend development/test install instruction (currently `pip install -r requirements.txt` at line ~36) uses requirements-dev.txt. Any README text that says requirements.txt includes test tools is corrected. `npm install` at line ~44 is left as is unless the implementer judges it a CI-style install, since the request limits README edits to the pip command. CLAUDE.md is NOT edited.
`npm ci && npm run build && npm test` pass in frontend/. frontend/package.json and package-lock.json are unchanged.
No other files change. App code, tests, and versions are unchanged.

assumptions.a: httpx placement: grep of backend/ shows httpx appears only in requirements.txt. It is imported nowhere in backend/app and nowhere in backend/tests. Tests use TestClient or AsyncClient (conftest.py, test_rules_postgres.py, test_api_symbols.py). Starlette's TestClient requires httpx, so httpx is test-only and goes in requirements-dev.txt. Note: the request's runtime list says "httpx if used at runtime", and it is not.
If the venv has httpx installed (the tests need it), its installed version is pinned. If the venv lacks httpx, the implementer must stop and report instead of choosing a version.
Only direct dependencies are pinned, matching the existing file style. A full transitive lock (pip-compile) is out of scope.
The repo-root .venv is assumed to be the Python 3.12 environment the suite passes in. CI and Docker use 3.12.
The implementer picks the postgres 16 minor tag. It must be a real, published tag, and the same string is used in both files.

The frontend Dockerfile change (copying package-lock.json) is required for "uses npm ci" and is not scope creep. Backend Dockerfile needs no change because it already references only requirements.txt.
The `[standard]` extra on uvicorn is kept. Its pin applies to uvicorn only.

edge_cases.e: pip freeze shows uvicorn without the extra. The pin is still `uvicorn[standard]==x`.
pydantic-settings and pydantic version compatibility: pin the exact pair from the venv.
`-r requirements.txt` in the dev file resolves relative to the dev file, so it works from any cwd and in CI (working-directory backend).
CI pip cache keyed only on requirements.txt would miss dev changes. Include both files in cache-dependency-path.
Windows line endings and a trailing newline: keep the files plain, one requirement per line.
The pinned versions must still be installable on Linux Python 3.12 (CI). Nothing in the pins should be Windows-specific.

risks.risk: The venv may contain versions that differ from what CI previously resolved. Pinning could expose a latent incompatibility on Linux. Mitigation: criterion 5 fresh-venv verification.
Docker build with npm ci fails if package-lock.json is out of sync with package.json. Criterion 11 checks this.
Pinned Postgres minor tag typo or nonexistent tag breaks compose and CI.
Moving httpx out of the runtime file would break anything that imports it at runtime. Grep shows nothing does.

spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: pinning (1,3,4), runtime-only image (2,8), dev file (3,5,6), Postgres tag (7), npm ci (6,9,11). All criteria are mechanically checkable. The biggest uncertainty is whether the venv really has the 33-pass environment and whether httpx is installed there. The "pin exact versions" requirement cannot be verified without running pip freeze, which the planner could not do. Also unconfirmed: whether the README should have its `npm install` line changed. The request only mandates the pip line, so that is left optional.
